title: Safety-net operator: Terraform module for private EKS control plane provisioning
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a hardened Terraform module and accompanying operator pattern (safety-net operator) to provision, upgrade, and verify Redwood Private EKS control planes in customer VPCs. The module must expose clear preflight hooks, automated health checks, and safe canary upgrade paths so Private customers have deterministic upgrades and self-healing probes without manual intervention.
terraform_module_interface: variables: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, control_plane_instance_type, kms_key_id (optional), maintenance_window, upgrade_strategy (canary|serial|bluegreen)
outputs: control_plane_endpoint, cluster_ca, managed_role_arn, upgrade_plan_id, last_preflight_report_s3_path
acceptance_criteria: Module can create a Private EKS control plane in a customer VPC with tags and encryption configured
Preflight checks run and produce a machine-readable report before apply; failure halts upgrades
Canary upgrade path can be triggered and rolled back automatically if health SLOs breach within the canary window
Operator reconciler detects control plane drift and executes configured auto-repair or creates an actionable incident
Smoke tests (API reachability, node bootstrap, kube-apiserver latency under 95th percentile threshold) pass in <= 15 minutes post-provision
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfooding on staging clusters; Terraform module under feature flag (2 clusters)
Phase 2: limited customer opt-in canary for 3 customers behind Redwood Dedicated contract
Phase 3: enable default for new Private deployments and document upgrade windows
Rollback criteria: any canary with >1 critical alert or >5% API error rate triggers automatic rollback
preflight_checks: IAM role validation and permissions scan
Subnet route table and NAT checks for control-plane communication
KMS key accessibility test and crypto policy validation
Existing cluster name collision and resource quota checks
Network CIDR overlap and egress policy probe
healthchecks: etcd quorum and compaction age alarms
control-plane node healthy count and CPU/memory headroom
periodic control-plane reconciliation summary written to S3 and Console
observability_hooks: emit per-deployment metrics: control_plane_provision_duration_seconds, upgrade_rollout_success_total, preflight_failures_total
traceable upgrade runs with trace IDs injected into Terraform output
Console dashboard: per-cluster upgrade history, last preflight snapshot, and top failing checks
alerting: PagerDuty for critical failures, Slack channel #priv-controlplane-upgrades for warnings
rollback_playbook: Step 1: Mark canary cohort unhealthy via console toggle
Step 2: Trigger automated rollback job using stored upgrade_plan_id
Step 3: Post-rollback validation: run smoke tests and post a rollback report to S3
Step 4: Open incident with RCA checklist if rollback occurred; attach preflight and healthcheck logs
